Preconditions: Staff test account ashish1660webmob+13@gmail.com exists and is used for staff-role testing throughout this project.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Go to /login. 2. Select Centre = 'Main Centre'. 3. Enter email ashish1660webmob+13@gmail.com and correct password. 4. Click 'Sign In'. 5. Observe error. 6. Change Centre to 'Sub Centre' (same credentials, no other change). 7. Click 'Sign In' again.
Expected Result: Staff account should successfully authenticate against whichever centre it is actually assigned to, and land on /dashboard.
Actual Result: Both attempts fail with the identical alert: "Your account is not assigned to this centre. Please select your centre and try again." The account cannot log in under either of the only two centres that exist in this environment (Main Centre, Sub Centre) - there is no third option to try. This fully explains the persistent staff-login failures observed throughout the automated Playwright suite (Phase 1 and Phase 2), which had been treated as an unexplained external blocker until now. IMPORTANT ADDITIONAL FINDING: checking Users Management (/users) shows this exact email does NOT appear anywhere in the user list, while a DIFFERENT, genuinely active staff account exists: 'Satff user1' <ashishwebmob1990@gmail.com>, role=staff, status=active. This strongly suggests the project's configured staff test credential (STAFF_EMAIL in .env, used throughout the automated Playwright framework) is simply the wrong/stale account, not a real centre-assignment defect - the actually-provisioned staff account is a different email entirely. Recommend the QA/dev team confirm the correct staff credential and update .env accordingly.

Steps to Reproduce: 1. Go to /login, leave Email empty, submit -> note error text under the field. 2. Go to /forgot-password, leave Email empty, submit -> note error text under the field. 3. Compare the two email input placeholders and the two error messages.
Expected Result: Consistent placeholder text and consistent validation wording for the same logical field (email) across pages of the same app.
Actual Result: Login page email placeholder is "you@company.com" and its empty/invalid-email error is "Enter a valid email". Forgot Password page email placeholder is "you@shriji.com" and its empty/invalid-email error is "Enter a valid email address". Also, both pages show the same wording for a genuinely empty field as for a malformed one ("Enter a valid email[...]"), which is slightly misleading copy for the empty-field case.

Feature: Console error logging on expected/handled failures
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Go to /login and submit valid centre/email with a wrong password. 2. Open browser console. 3. Separately: while logged out, navigate directly to /dashboard by URL and open the console.
Expected Result: Expected, user-facing, already-handled failure conditions (wrong password -> shown as an inline alert; unauthenticated silent-refresh attempt before redirecting to /login) should not also be logged to the console as console.error - that channel should be reserved for genuinely unexpected failures.
Actual Result: Both cases log real console.error() entries ("Failed to load resource: ... 401", "[ERROR] [API] API Error 401", "[ERROR] [QueryClient] Mutation error AxiosError: Request failed with status code 401") even though the UI already handles the condition correctly. This adds noise to the console and would cause any CI check that fails a build on console.error output to false-positive on completely normal user flows (wrong password, session expiry).

Module/Page: Admission / Add New Admission (and Edit Admission)
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Go to Admission > Add New Admission. 2. Fill all required fields with valid data EXCEPT type 'abcdefghij' (10 letters, no digits) into the Mobile field. 3. Fill Father's Mobile with a real 10-digit number. 4. Observe the Mobile field's validation state clears once exactly 10 characters are present. 5. Click 'Submit Admission'.
Expected Result: Mobile and Father's Mobile should be validated as actual numeric phone numbers (10 digits, digits only) both client-side and server-side; a value like 'abcdefghij' should be rejected with an error and the record should not be saved.
Actual Result: The client-side validation only checks string length (exactly 10 characters) and does not check that the characters are digits - the invalid-state indicator and 'Enter 10-digit mobile number' error disappear once 10 characters of any kind are entered. The form submits successfully and the record is saved to the backend with Mobile = 'abcdefghij' (confirmed: admission PW-ADM-QAE2E5981 was created and appeared in the Admissions list with status 'Confirmed'). This is a genuine end-to-end data-integrity gap - the backend enforces no numeric-mobile validation either. The same unvalidated Mobile field is also editable (not locked) on the Edit Admission form, so the corrupted value can persist and be re-edited indefinitely.

Feature: Numeric field default state (Fees Paid, Final Fees)
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Go to Admission > Add New Admission. 2. Immediately open the browser console (before interacting with the form).
Expected Result: No console warnings on a fresh page load with no user interaction.
Actual Result: Two identical console warnings fire immediately on page load: "The specified value 'NaN' cannot be parsed, or is out of range." This points to the 'Fees Paid' and 'Final Fees' numeric spinbuttons being initialized with an uncontrolled/NaN internal value before the user types anything, rather than an empty string or 0. The same pattern reproduces on the Add New Installment form (/installments/new) - clicking 'Reset' there fires the identical warning 3 times, suggesting the same numeric-field pattern is reused across Final Fee/Remaining Fee/Fees.

Expected Result: Only real, intentional course names should appear in the dropdown.
Actual Result: The dropdown's first option is a junk/garbage entry: "12333333)))((((&&&&&##@@!!" - clearly test data that was entered into the Course master list (Settings) and never cleaned up. Preconditions: Logged in as admin. An admission with a non-zero remaining balance exists (used PW-ADM-MRC3TKO34AK, Remaining Fee ₹22,000).
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Go to Installments > Add New Installment. 2. Enter the Admission Number and let the rest auto-fill. 3. Select Payment Method = Cash. 4. Type '0' into the Fees field. 5. Observe the field's validation state and the Submit Installment button.
Expected Result: A ₹0 installment payment is not a meaningful business record and should be rejected with a validation error (e.g. 'Fees must be greater than 0'), consistent with the Admission form's own 'Must be greater than 0' rule for its Fees Paid field.
Actual Result: Entering 0 shows no invalid state and no error message, and the 'Submit Installment' button becomes enabled (not disabled) - the same field correctly blocks values ABOVE the remaining balance ('Fees cannot exceed the remaining fee') but does not block 0. Not submitted to avoid creating a meaningless ₹0 test record, but the enabled Submit button is sufficient evidence the client-side gate would allow it through.
